{{short description|Russian-American mathematician}}
'''Alexander Nikolaevich Dranishnikov''' (Александр Николаевич Дранишников; born  5 February 1958) is a Russian-American mathematician, focusing in geometry and topology, currently a distinguished professor at the [[University of Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://fora.aa.ufl.edu/provost/IndependentFora/Distinguished-Professors |title=Alexander Dranishnikov |publisher=ufl.edu |access-date=May 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://people.clas.ufl.edu/dranish/ |title=Alexander Dranishnikov |publisher=ufl.edu |access-date=May 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=X-xgQn0AAAAJ&hl=en |title=Alexander Dranishnikov |access-date=May 12, 2017}}</ref> In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Dranishnikov, A. N.|chapter=Dimension theory and large Riemannian manifolds|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians|volume=2|pages=423–432|year=1998|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011698000}}</ref> In 2012 he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2017-08-09.</ref>
